question: For a 34%/8.2 psia lunar habitat, which PSI investigations matter most and why?
answer: Ranking for 34% O₂ at 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia), 5 cm/s: 1. FLEX (score 0.63; liquid fuels (cabin materials are mostly solids); 275 verified test points in EmberAtlas) 2. BASS (score 0.45; solid fuels (cabin materials are mostly solids); 0 verified test points in EmberAtlas) 3. BASS-II (score 0.42; solid fuels (cabin materials are mostly solids); 0 verified test points in EmberAtlas) 4. Saffire-IV-VI (score 0.41; solid fuels (cabin materials are mostly solids); 0 verified test points in EmberAtlas) No PSI investigation tested 34%/56.5 kPa directly, so atmosphere match is partial for all [S:psi]. FLEX ranks high because it is the only investigation with verified test points in EmberAtlas so far [S:ntrs-20150023456]; solid-fuel campaigns (BASS-II, Saffire) score on fuel realism and scale [S:bass2-sci-rep-2017] [S:ntrs-20180005168]. See /evidence.

question: Can PMMA burn at lower O₂ in microgravity than in a 1 g test? Show the evidence and the model.
answer: BASS-II reports a lower limiting O₂ for PMMA rods in microgravity than in normal gravity: Limiting O2 for PMMA rods was lower in microgravity (about 17%) than in normal gravity (about 18%) (value to verify). [S:bass2-sci-rep-2017]. The mechanism is flow: at low imposed flow, µg flames avoid the strong buoyant convection that blows off or cools 1 g flames. EmberAtlas cannot yet show a model boundary for this — the flammability-boundary model [M:boundary] is not built because BASS-II burn/extinct points still need digitization — so this is evidence, not a model output. Conflicting evidence: quiescent µg flames are weaker (BRE) [S:dehghani-bre]. See /gaps.

question: Estimate the opposed-flow spread rate over 0.37 mm SIBAL fabric at 34% O₂, 8.2 psia, 10 cm/s, in lunar gravity, with uncertainty.
answer: [M:spread] gives 4.58 mm/s (p05–p95 3.55–5.88) for SIBAL at 34% O₂ (pO₂ 19.2 kPa), 56.5 kPa, 10 cm/s forced flow. Lunar buoyancy adds u_b ≈ 24.2 cm/s, so the equivalent flow is 34.2 cm/s; the band [µg, g-equivalent] is 4.58–4.58 mm/s — a bounded estimate, not a measurement [S:olson-1991]. Thin-fuel de Ris spread does not depend on flow, so the two ends coincide. This is uncalibrated — theory only (BASS-II/Saffire data pending) [S:de-ris-1969]. See /models/spread.

question: How much CO₂ (mole fraction) would be needed to inert a heptane fire at 21%/14.7 psia vs 34%/8.2 psia? Compare 1 g and µg calibrations.
answer: [M:suppression], CO₂ dispersed into the cabin atmosphere: at 21% O₂ / 101.3 kPa the µg-calibrated answer is 0.197 mole fraction (p05–p95 0.181–0.211) vs 0.225 with the 1 g reference. At 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa it is 0.438 (p05–p95 0.425–0.449) vs 0.459 (1 g). µg T_crit is 1963 K (fitted to FLEX O₂/N₂ LOIs) and the 1 g reference 1900 K [S:dietrich-2014] [S:nfpa-2001]. The 56.5 kPa case is outside validated range (FLEX LOIs are at 1 atm). See /models/suppression.

question: What is heptane's droplet LOI, and how does CO₂ dilution change it?
answer: FLEX measured a heptane LOI of about 0.15 in O₂/N₂ at 1 atm, rising to about 0.17 when CO₂ is dispersed into air [S:dietrich-2014]. EmberAtlas' droplet dual-extinction model predicts 0.1143 and 0.1306 (fail, reported) [M:droplet], while pure thermal theory with a µg T_crit fitted on the O₂/N₂ LOI predicts 0.1686 for CO₂ (pass) [M:suppression]. So CO₂ raises the limiting O₂ mainly through its heat capacity. See /validation.

question: Do flames survive without ventilation at 34% O₂? (BRE + boundary model)
answer: ACME BRE evidence: Flames extinguished at 21% O2 within about 40 s; steady flames were observed at 26.5, 34 and 40% O2 (to verify). [S:dehghani-bre]. So at 34% O₂ quiescent flames were observed to persist in that burner configuration, while at 21% they extinguished. The boundary model [M:boundary] is not available yet (no digitized solid burn/extinct data), so EmberAtlas gives no probability here. See /gaps.

question: A 5 kW fire burns 3 minutes in a 20 m³ rover: what happens to cabin T, P, O₂ and CO₂?
answer: [M:habitat] for a 5 kW cotton fire, 180 s, 20 m³ at 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa: at the end of the burn the cabin is 47.3 °C and 60.9 kPa; O₂ falls to 33.4% and CO₂ rises to 0.453%, CO 17.6 ppm. Peak temperature rise 22.3 K (p05–p95 6.6–31.9). O₂ consumption uses 13.1 MJ/kg O₂ [S:huggett-1980]; limits from JSC 20584 [S:jsc-20584-revC]. Uncalibrated — theory only (wall heat loss not yet fitted to Saffire). See /models/habitat.

question: Is there lunar-gravity data in PSI? (Answer: no; explain the bounding method.)
answer: No. PSI combustion data are microgravity or 1 g; EmberAtlas holds 0 partial-gravity points [S:psi]. We bound lunar behaviour with an equivalent flow: u_b = (g α ΔT/T)^(1/3) gives 24.2 cm/s at lunar g for 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa, so a 5 cm/s fan flow maps to 29.2 cm/s [M:gravity] [S:olson-1991]. The result is a band between µg and that equivalent flow — a bounded estimate, never a measurement. LUCI and FM2 are external cross-checks (outside PSI) [S:ntrs-20240015307]. See /console.

question: Is helium or CO₂ the better suppressant in microgravity?
answer: The evidence conflicts. FLEX droplets: CO₂ raised heptane's LOI to about 0.17 while helium gave about 0.15 [S:dietrich-2014]. Pure thermal theory [M:suppression] needs 0.197 mole fraction CO₂ vs 0.388 He to inert heptane in air, ranking CO₂ more effective per mole — but it under-predicts FLEX He LOIs (predicted 0.1286, fail), pointing to helium's diffusivity. A drop-tower study found helium most effective (outside PSI) [S:drop-tower-suppressant]. Treat it as configuration-dependent. See /gaps.

question: Where is the evidence thinnest for lunar habitats, and what 5 tests would most reduce uncertainty?
answer: Thinnest evidence: no partial-gravity data (0 points) and no verified solid-fuel data at 34% O₂ / 56.5 kPa; verified points are FLEX droplets only [S:ntrs-20150023456]. Proposed tests (coverage-based heuristic (GP/BALD pending boundary data)): 1. SIBAL at 34% O₂, 56.5 kPa, 0.5 cm/s; 2. SIBAL at 34% O₂, 56.5 kPa, 2 cm/s; 3. SIBAL at 34% O₂, 56.5 kPa, 5 cm/s; 4. PMMA at 34% O₂, 56.5 kPa, 10 cm/s; 5. SIBAL at 32% O₂, 56.5 kPa, 0.5 cm/s. Target rig: SoFIE (rig limits to verify) [S:psi]. See /gaps.

question: Compare BASS-II and Saffire on SIBAL fabric: what changes with scale?
answer: BASS-II burned small samples in a glovebox duct at 0.4–8 cm/s and reduced O₂ [S:bass2-sci-rep-2017]; Saffire burned a large SIBAL sheet in a Cygnus vehicle at 20–25 cm/s in air [S:ntrs-20180005168]. Scale changes flame length, radiation and heat feedback, so small-sample spread rates need not transfer to large fires. Quantitative comparison awaits digitized SIBAL spread rates from both (listed in HUMAN_TASKS). See /evidence.
